title: Quantum holography and associative chiral Koszul duality
subtitle: Ordered collisions, chiral quantum groups, and the relation between boundary operators and bulk theories.
lead: Associative chiral Koszul duality studies singular composition with the order of the inputs retained. Its constructions include coefficient systems on configurations, vertex algebras, quantum vertex algebras, and module categories with fusion. Bar and cobar relate multiplication to coherent comultiplication. A realization by fields must also specify the collision maps, completion, local vacuum, and module tensor product.

The programme has coefficient dualities, explicit field duals, algebraic bulk operations, and restricted fusion theorems. Several comparisons now hold on full algebraic state spaces or at every finite configuration arity. Their hypotheses distinguish polynomial states, completed inputs, ordinary derived categories, and categories defined by different weak equivalences.

The remaining questions compare independently defined constructions. They concern native collision operations, common completed fusion domains, geometric bulk actions, and states prepared by physical amplitudes. A complementary-level partner, a bar dual, and a vacuum endomorphism algebra retain separate definitions.

The table gives the available results and the unresolved comparison for each example. The questions below state the mathematical data needed to extend them. A partial theorem retains its positive domain even when a stronger comparison fails.

principal.title: Siegel–Weil for the hyperbolic genus
principal.text: Let \(V\) be a strongly rational holomorphic vertex operator algebra over \(\mathbb C\), with its conformal vector, algebraic graded direct-sum states, a chosen Cartan subalgebra of \(V_1\), strongly rational Heisenberg commutant \(C\), and associated positive-definite even lattice of rank \(r\ge3\). Write \(c=c(V)\), let \(\mathcal H(V)\) be its hyperbolic genus, let \(G_W\) be the finite image of the Cartan-preserving automorphisms of \(W\) on its associated lattice, and put \(m(V)=\sum_{[W]\in\mathcal H(V)}|G_W|^{-1}\). For \(r>4\) and \(\tau\) in the upper half-plane, \[\frac{1}{m(V)}\sum_{[W]\in\mathcal H(V)}\frac{\operatorname{ch}_W(\tau)}{|G_W|}=\sum_{\gamma\in\Gamma_\infty\backslash\operatorname{SL}_2(\mathbb Z)}\varepsilon(\gamma)^c\frac{\operatorname{ch}_C(\gamma\tau)}{\eta(\gamma\tau)^r},\qquad \Gamma_\infty=\{\pm T^n:n\in\mathbb Z\}.\] Here \(\eta\) is the Dedekind eta function and \(\varepsilon\) its standard multiplier, with metaplectic lifts when required; the sum is absolutely and locally uniformly convergent. At \(r=3,4\), multiply each summand by \(\operatorname{Im}(\gamma\tau)^t\), continue meromorphically from \(\operatorname{Re}t>1-r/4\), and evaluate at \(t=0\): the standard section specified by the real Gaussian and finite lattice-coset characteristic functions is regular there and has the same value, with the metaplectic convention at rank three. The proof uses the positive nonvacuum commutant weights supplied by Dong–Sun–Wang’s 2026 preprint; assuming those weights are strictly positive is an explicit alternative hypothesis. For this holomorphic class this establishes, in the absolutely convergent range \(r>4\), the character identity of Möller–Rayhaun, arXiv:2408.07117 (2024), Conjecture 5.7; at \(r=3,4\) the identity holds for the specified continuation. The arithmetic Siegel–Weil theorems are known inputs.
principal.antecedents: Möller–Rayhaun (2024), arXiv:2408.07117, Conjecture 5.7, Theorem 4.7 and Corollary 4.11; van Ekeren–Möller–Scheithauer (2015, preprint), Theorem 4.2; Dong–Sun–Wang (2026, preprint), arXiv:2611.12417, Theorem 3 and Corollary 5.3; Opitz (2018), Theorem 3.7.2; Kudla (2001, preprint), arXiv:math/0110236, Theorem 4.1(i) and Proposition 4.22.

principal.title: Associative bar–cobar duality with finite arity filtrations
principal.text: Let \(X\) be a smooth separated finite-type curve over a characteristic-zero field \(k\), and equip \(\mathcal S_X=D(k)\times\prod_{n\geq1}\operatorname{DMod}(X^n)\) with consecutive-cut convolution, using unbounded right algebraic differential modules with quasi-coherent underlying modules and derived external tensors. Bar and cobar give inverse equivalences between augmented coherent associative algebras with \(A_0\simeq k\) and counital coaugmented coherent coassociative coalgebras with \(C_0\simeq k\), including mapping spaces; each reduced word at arity \(n\) has length at most \(n\), so no cohomological boundedness assumption is needed. These equivalences restrict to algebras whose positive-arity coefficients vanish on every separated cut and strong cut coalgebras. For such a coalgebra, \(\overline{\Omega C}_n\simeq R\Gamma_{Z_n}(C_n)[-1]\), where \(Z_1=X\) and \(Z_n=\bigcap_{p=1}^{n-1}\bigcup_{i\leq p<j}\Delta_{ij}\) for \(n\geq2\); in particular, \(Z_3=\Delta_{13}\).

principal.title: Curved duality for universal affine and Virasoro modes
principal.text: Over discrete \(\mathbb C\), take the universal affine algebra of a finite-dimensional simple \(\mathfrak g\), with \(\operatorname{Kill}=2h^\vee(\ ,\ )\), at any level \(\kappa\), or the universal Virasoro algebra at any charge \(c\), in a fixed formal coordinate. For \(\mathfrak t=\mathfrak g((z))\) or \(\mathbb C((z))\partial_z\), with \(L_n=-z^{n+1}\partial_z\), choose the positive subalgebra \(\mathfrak p=\mathfrak g[[z]]\) or \(\prod_{n\geq0}\mathbb C L_n\), respectively, and exhaust its discrete complement by finite-dimensional spaces \(D_m\); the curved ghost algebra is \(B_\eta=\varprojlim_m(\Lambda\mathfrak p^\vee\otimes\Lambda D_m^*,d_{\rm CE},+\eta)\), with \(\eta(xz^m,yz^n)=\kappa m(x,y)\delta_{m+n,0}\) or \(\eta(L_m,L_n)=c(m^3-m)\delta_{m+n,0}/12\), and the limit is degreewise, with finite positive support allowed to vary with the negative-mode subset and no product over exterior degrees. Smoothness means that each vector is killed by some positive-mode tail; smooth complexes modulo those coacyclic on \(\mathfrak p\) are equivalent to graded-projective curved \(B_\eta\)-contramodules modulo those with Becker-coacyclic positive quotient; passing to ordinary derived smooth modules requires the further quotient by objects whose inverse image is acyclic. Complementary categorical duality has parameters \(-\kappa-2h^\vee\) and \(26-c\), including critical level, while the algebraic dual is the curved ghost algebra just described; simple integrable and minimal-model quotients are outside this theorem.

principal.title: The spectral bar comparison on augmentation-generated categories
principal.text: Let \(H\) be an augmented dg bialgebra over a characteristic-zero field \(k\), with strict dg coproduct and a degree-zero locally nilpotent algebra derivation and coalgebra coderivation \(T\) satisfying \([d_H,T]=0\) and \(\varepsilon T=0\). Use the direct-sum normalized bar resolution, full-product Hom cochains \(C(M)=R\operatorname{Hom}_H(k,M)\), and \(B=C(k)\); for \(s\in k\), the translated coproduct \(\Delta_s=(e^{sT}\otimes1)\Delta\) gives a natural comparison \(C(M)\otimes_B^{\mathbf L}{}_{\Theta_s}C(N)\longrightarrow C(M\otimes_sN)\), where \(\Theta_s\) translates the bar inputs and twists the second left \(B\)-action. This map is an equivalence whenever either input belongs to \(\operatorname{thick}(k)\subset D(H)\), and cochains identify \(\operatorname{thick}(k)\) with \(\operatorname{Perf}(B)\), with coherent translated products and units. If the augmentation module \(k\) is compact in \(D(H)\), the equivalence extends to \(\operatorname{Loc}(k)\simeq D(B)\); compactness alone does not make \(k\) generate all of \(D(H)\).

principal.title: Formal higher cohomology on the Hilbert scheme
principal.text: For \(N\geq1\), let \(\mathcal D\) be the Arakawa–Kuwabara–Möller formal vertex-superalgebra sheaf obtained by framed \(\mathfrak{gl}_N\) BRST reduction of adjoint and fundamental symplectic bosons with fundamental fermions on \(M_N=\operatorname{Hilb}^N(\mathbb C^2)\), over \(R=\mathbb C[[\hbar]]\): each of \(\mathcal D\) and \(\mathcal D/\hbar^m\mathcal D\), \(m\geq1\), has nonzero sheaf cohomology exactly in degrees \(0,\ldots,N-1\). For \(N\geq2\), its normal-cup subalgebra generated by the vacuum and translated determinant classes is \((R\otimes_{\mathbb C}\Lambda(e_0,e_1,\ldots))/(\hbar e_r,\Lambda^{\geq N})\), with only finite sums and products in the generators. Here \(e_r\) has sheaf degree one, intrinsic even parity and conformal weight \(r+1\); increasing products of fewer than \(N\) generators are nonzero, not \(\hbar\)-divisible, and have independent nonzero images in every finite \(\hbar\) quotient. These positive-degree classes vanish after taking the torus-finite part and then specializing \(\hbar=1\).

principal.title: Minimal-model fusion with a finite-base fibre
principal.text: Let \(2\leq p<q\) be coprime, set \(c_{p,q}=1-6(p-q)^2/(pq)\), and let \(\mathcal C_{p,q}\) be the complex linear category of finite direct sums of simple \(L(c_{p,q},0)\)-modules, with the simple vacuum as tensor unit. If \(I\) indexes its simple modules, the functor \(F(M)=\bigoplus_{i,j\in I}\operatorname{Hom}(L_i,M\boxtimes L_j)\) is exact, faithful and strong monoidal into finite \(\mathbb C^I\)-bimodules, using tensor product over \(\mathbb C^I\). The finite weak Hopf algebra \(H=\bigoplus_{a\in I}\operatorname{End}_{\mathbb C}(F(L_a))\) reconstructs the ribbon category and its full rational Ward output, with module tensor product \(\Delta(1)(V\otimes W)\), where \(\Delta(1)\) projects onto matching intermediate labels. Its canonical finite pairing tensor satisfies both coproduct pairing laws and the categorical exchange identity; its scalar counit need not be multiplicative.

principal.title: Abelian bulk sources give full boundary Fock modules
principal.text: On \(M=\mathbb C_z\times\mathbb R_{\geq0}\), oriented by \(dx\wedge dy\wedge dt\), fix \(\kappa\in\mathbb C^\times\) and let \(A(U)\) be compactly supported differential forms whose boundary pullback lies in \(dz\wedge\Omega_c^\bullet(U\cap\partial M)\). The Gaussian observables \(\bigoplus_{m\geq0}\operatorname{Sym}_b^m(A(U)[2])\) use completed projective bornological tensors at each field number, an algebraic sum over field numbers, and the BV pairing \(-\kappa(2\pi i)^{-1}\int_U a\wedge b\). For a proper vertical ray \(L\) beginning at the boundary and charge \(\alpha\in\mathbb C\), the supported source differential is \(d+\Delta_\kappa-i\alpha I_L\), where \(I_L(a)=\int_La\) on spatial one-forms and is zero on other linear degrees; its rotation-finite endpoint cohomology is concentrated in degree zero and equals \(\mathcal F_\alpha=\mathbb C[J_{-1},J_{-2},\ldots]|\alpha\rangle\). The complete current action is \(J_{-n}=x_n\), \(J_n=\kappa n\partial_{x_n}\) for \(n>0\), and \(J_0=\alpha\), on algebraic polynomial states.

principal.title: A strict dg bi-Galois object for exterior uncurving marks
principal.text: Let \(k\) be a characteristic-zero field, let \(r\ge0\) be finite, and let \(H=\Lambda(\theta_1,\ldots,\theta_r)\) have primitive degree-one generators and zero differential. Work with algebraic, possibly unbounded dg modules and direct-sum tensor totalization. If \(N_i\) is the action of \(\theta_i\), an uncurving mark \(\lambda\in k^r\) replaces a module differential \(D\) by \(D-\sum_i\lambda_iN_i\); let \(W_\lambda\) be the maps that become quasi-isomorphisms after this replacement. For \(K=\Lambda(\xi_1,\ldots,\xi_r)\), with primitive generators of degree \(-1\) and zero differential, and \(a\in k^r\), \[L_a=\bigl(\Lambda(\eta_1,\ldots,\eta_r),\ d\eta_i=a_i\bigr),\qquad |\eta_i|=-1,\] with the primitive left and right translation coactions of \(K\), is a strict dg bi-Galois object. Its coinvariants are \(k\), both canonical maps are dg isomorphisms, and algebraic cotensor by \(L_a\) sends \((M,D)\) to \((M,D-\sum_i a_iN_i)\). For \(a=\lambda-\mu\) this gives a monoidal equivalence of the localizations defined by \(W_\lambda\) and \(W_\mu\), with \(L_a\mathbin{\square}_K L_b\cong L_{a+b}\), unit \(L_0\), and inverse \(L_{-a}\). If \(a\ne0\), the underlying complex of \(L_a\) is acyclic, so this statement uses strict cotensor and the specified marked localizations.

principal.title: Reconstruction from an admissible geometric vacuum
principal.text: Let \(X\) be a smooth algebraic curve over \(\mathbb C\). Suppose a category-valued system, varying under arbitrary parameter pullback, \(\mathcal C_I\) on every \(X^I\), including \(\mathcal C_\varnothing=\operatorname{Vect}_{\mathbb C}\), has coherent pullback functors for all finite-set maps, equivalences for surjections, unit insertions for injections, and symmetric external fusion over disjoint configurations, satisfying composition, iterated-partition and mixed base-change identities. Let its vacua \(v_I\) come from the empty unit, and let \(F_I:\mathcal C_I\to\operatorname{QCoh}(X^I)\) be compatible \(\mathcal O\)-linear realizations whose vacuum comparisons for surjections and disjoint fusion are invertible. Require \(B_I=F_I(v_I)\) to have no nonzero local sections supported on collision diagonals and \(B_\varnothing\cong\mathbb C\) as an algebra with its actual unit. Then \(B_I\) is a factorization algebra, and its canonical connection and residue operation reconstruct a unital chiral algebra on the right differential module \(\omega_X\otimes B_{\{1\}}\), with all operadic substitutions. Equivalences preserving these realized vacuum diagrams give isomorphic unital chiral algebras. On \(\mathbb A^1\), translation-equivariant input gives the corresponding vertex algebra; an explicitly retained conformal vector and grading are preserved. This is the Beilinson–Drinfeld reconstruction applied to the specified geometric coefficients.

questions.title: The native operations of the affine bulk

question.title: Lift the affine state operations to configurations
question.text: Let \(k\) have characteristic zero, let \(\mathfrak g\) be finite-dimensional, let \(\kappa\) be an invariant symmetric form, and suppose \(\beta=\kappa+\operatorname{Kill}_{\mathfrak g}/2\) is nondegenerate. On the universal polynomial affine Chevalley–Eilenberg complex \(Z=V^\kappa(\mathfrak g)\otimes\Lambda(c_n^a:n\ge0)\), construct a configuration-indexed dg system of regular, localized and supported chiral operations that realizes the specified closed degree-minus-two secondary bracket, its full shifted Lie operations, the native normally ordered product and an independently specified boundary action. Retain joint formal zero modes in the geometric coefficients, polynomial positive-energy states, the algebraic sum over energies, ordered mergers and vacuum insertions, and prove every mixed Leibniz, Jacobi and action coherence. Compare this realization with the independently defined geometric roof pairing, including its prescribed nullhomotopy on separated configurations and compatibility with both nested and disjoint collisions.

questions.why: A structure on the vector space of states does not specify how insertions move, collide or act on boundary modules. The comparison would identify which higher operations belong to the geometric bulk and whether they agree with the pairing obtained from the boundary construction.

known.title: Energy retraction and lifting of algebraic operations
known.text: Over a characteristic-zero field \(k\), suppose \(Z=\bigoplus_{e\ge0}Z_e\), the differential preserves energy, \(A_0=Z_0\), and inclusion \(i\), projection \(p\), and an energy-preserving degree-minus-one map \(H\) satisfy \(H|_{A_0}=0\) and \(dH+Hd=1-ip\). Using full algebraic graded Hom, restriction \[\operatorname{End}_Z^{E}\longrightarrow\operatorname{End}_{A_0}\] from energy-additive operations is an aritywise surjective quasi-isomorphism of unital dg operads, including arity zero; its kernel is contracted by \(f\mapsto Hf\). No finite-dimensionality or condition \(H^2=0\) is required. For finite-dimensional \(\mathfrak g\) and invariant symmetric \(\kappa\) with nondegenerate \(\beta=\kappa+\operatorname{Kill}/2\), the universal polynomial affine complex \(Z=V^\kappa(\mathfrak g)\otimes\Lambda(c_n^a)\) has these data with \(A_0=C^*(\mathfrak g;k)\), \(H=K_E/e\) at positive energy, \(H=0\) at energy zero, and \(K_E=[L_1,K]/2\), where \([d,K]=T\). Only the shifted form \(\beta\) is inverted.

known.title: Rigidity with the marked operations held fixed
known.text: Over a characteristic-zero field, let \(Z=\bigoplus_{e\ge0}Z_e\) retract onto \(A_0=Z_0\) by energy-preserving \(i,p,H\), with \(H|_{A_0}=0\) and \(dH+Hd=1-ip\), and use full algebraic graded Hom. Fix a relative cofibration \(Q^{\prime}\hookrightarrow Q\) of dg operads, a \(Q\)-action on \(A_0\), and an energy-additive \(Q^{\prime}\)-action on \(Z\) restricting to it. The action extends to \(Q\), and any two extensions are homotopic relative to \(Q^{\prime}\) and over the fixed \(Q\)-action on \(A_0\). A relative cellular presentation with a well-ordered exhaustive set of generators and each differential in earlier stages suffices; absolute cofibrancy alone does not express the marked relative requirement.
known.antecedents: Markl, Homotopy Algebras are Homotopy Algebras (2004), Definition 17, Theorem 19 and Lemma 20; Hinich (2003), corrected Theorem 3.2, including nullary operations.

known.title: The native binary operations admit algebraic higher coherences
known.text: Let \(\mathfrak g\) be finite-dimensional over a characteristic-zero field, with invariant symmetric \(\kappa\) and nondegenerate \(\beta=\kappa+\operatorname{Kill}/2\), and use the algebraic universal affine complex \(Z=V^\kappa(\mathfrak g)\otimes\Lambda(c_n^a)\). Any closed, energy-additive, vacuum-normalized, graded-skew degree-minus-two bracket \(b\) restricting to the inverse-\(\beta\) bracket on \(C^*(\mathfrak g)\) extends on the algebraic cofree conilpotent symmetric coalgebra \(S^c(Z[3])\) to shifted Lie operations of arity \(n\) and degree \(4-3n\), with the higher operations zero on constant ghosts and on vacuum inputs. For a fixed relative cofibrant resolution of the degree-minus-two Poisson operad, the native normally ordered product and \(b\) can both be held fixed, with all algebraic product, bracket and mixed coherences. The product generator has no imposed symmetry or associativity relation; in a resolution containing a degree-minus-three Leibniz cell, that cell can be assigned exactly \(HL_b\), where \(L_b\) is the Leibniz defect. An already specified full shifted Lie family and this first Leibniz primitive can also be retained by a relative resolution; the uniqueness is homotopy relative to those data, at the level of algebraic states.

known.title: Algebraic lifting with a boundary colour
known.text: Over a characteristic-zero field, let \(Z=\bigoplus_{e\ge0}Z_e\) retract onto \(A_0=Z_0\) by energy-preserving \(i,p,H\), with \(H|_{A_0}=0\) and \(dH+Hd=1-ip\), and let \(V\) be any cochain complex. Allow only bulk inputs for a bulk output, using energy-additive operations on \(Z\); allow arbitrary bulk and boundary inputs for a boundary output, using full algebraic graded Hom; set every boundary-input, bulk-output profile to zero. Restriction from \((Z,V)\) to \((A_0,V)\) is an aritywise and profilewise surjective quasi-isomorphism. An independently specified action of a cofibrant coloured operad with these profiles therefore lifts, uniquely up to homotopy over the entire fixed bulk, mixed and boundary action; preserving marked operations requires a relative cofibration. The inclusion \((i,1_V)\) is strict, while the projection need not be strict on boundary-output operations.

known.title: Transfer retains total weight zero
known.text: Over a characteristic-zero field, let \(Z=\bigoplus_{e\ge0}Z_e\) have an energy-preserving retraction \((i,p,H)\) onto \(A_0=Z_0\), with \(H|_{A_0}=0\) and \(dH+Hd=1-ip\). Let \(\mathcal O\) be an integer-weighted dg operad whose composition, differential, identity and augmentation \(\mathcal O\to\mathcal I\) preserve weight, with \(\mathcal I\) in weight zero, acting so that weight \(w\) shifts energy by \(w\). In the algebraic conilpotent reduced finite-tree bar \(B\mathcal O\), including unary and permitted nullary vertices, the sum \(I_{\ne0}\) of nonzero total weights is a dg coideal. Transfer gives a twisting morphism \(B\mathcal O/I_{\ne0}\to\operatorname{End}_{A_0}\) and a cobar action, with an infinity quasi-isomorphism to \(Z\) after pullback to \(\Omega B\mathcal O\). The quotient coproduct projects each factor to weight zero; it is not a claim that the weight-zero summand is a subcooperad. A strict unit and multiplication do not automatically admit the required augmentation.
known.antecedents: Van der Laan (2003), Theorem 5.2(i); Hoffbeck–Leray–Vallette (2021), Theorem 4.14 and §6.1; Berglund (2014), Theorem 1.3, with its narrower connectedness and side conditions.

known.title: A weight-zero bar composite gives the constant bracket
known.text: For the universal polynomial affine Chevalley–Eilenberg complex of a finite-dimensional Lie algebra over a characteristic-zero field, take an invariant symmetric level form \(\kappa\), assume \(\beta=\kappa+\operatorname{Kill}/2\) is nondegenerate and use the energy retraction \(H\). Let \(K\) be the Sugawara translation nullhomotopy, and let \(B_0\) be the raw constant coefficient of the specified two-copy pairing, and let \(C_0(a,v)=(-1)^{|a|+1}B_0(a,v)\) be the Hom-closed degree-minus-one, weight-minus-one signed constant pairing. If an integer-weighted augmented dg operad acts with each weight-\(w\) operation shifting total energy by \(w\), has weight-preserving augmentation and contains closed \(T,C_0\) with their weights \(1,-1\) and relation \(C_0\circ_1T=0\), then its signed bar cycle \(\theta=-[sC_0\mid sT]_1\), with bar suspension of degree minus one, transfers on constant ghosts to \[\alpha(\theta)(a,v)=pC_0(HTa,v)=C_0(Ka,v)=b_0(a,v).\] Here \(b_0\) is the degree-minus-two inverse-\(\beta\) bracket on \(C^*(\mathfrak g)\), and the equality uses \(HTa=Ka\) for \(a\in C^*(\mathfrak g)\); it identifies this composite and does not determine the whole weight-zero homology.

known.title: Reductive Poisson formality and the fixed affine action
known.text: Let \(\mathfrak g=\mathfrak z\oplus\mathfrak s\) be a finite-dimensional reductive Lie algebra over a characteristic-zero field \(k\), and let \(\beta\) be a nondegenerate invariant symmetric form. The inclusion \[((\Lambda\mathfrak g^*)^{\mathfrak g},0)\hookrightarrow(C^*(\mathfrak g;k),d_{\mathrm{CE}})\] is a strict dg Poisson quasi-isomorphism for the exterior product and the degree-minus-two inverse-\(\beta\) bracket. On \(\Lambda\mathfrak z^*\otimes(\Lambda\mathfrak s^*)^{\mathfrak s}\), the bracket is the inverse central form and vanishes identically on the semisimple invariant factor; this invariant-cochain vanishing is a known result. For the universal polynomial affine complex with \(\beta=\kappa+\operatorname{Kill}/2\), the same formality holds for an existing energy-additive action of a fixed cofibrant operad \(Q\) whose restriction factors through a fixed \(Q\to\mathrm{Pois}_3\) and this exact strict Poisson structure. It does not specify arbitrary additional operations or a boundary action, and for a nonzero centre the inverse central form remains part of the Poisson algebra.

known.title: The specified bracket is the average of two endpoint extractions
known.text: Let \(k\) have characteristic zero, let \(\mathfrak g\) be finite-dimensional with invariant symmetric \(\kappa\) and nondegenerate \(\beta=\kappa+\operatorname{Kill}/2\), and use the universal polynomial affine complex \(Z\). Write \(q_\lambda(a,b)=(-1)^{|a|}B_\lambda(a,b)\) for its Hom-closed degree-minus-one sesquilinear pairing and \([d,K]=T\) for the full Sugawara homotopy. After transporting the pairing by the gauge \(1+dzK\), use \(u_t=tz_1+(1-t)z_2\), \(w=z_1-z_2\), and extract the \(dw\) coefficient followed by normal derivative order zero. The resulting closed, energy-additive operation is \[C_t=-(1-t)q_{-tT}(K\otimes1)+tq_{-tT}(1\otimes K),\qquad b_{\mathrm{specified}}=\frac{C_0+C_1}{2},\] with the Koszul tensor signs. The midpoint \(C_{1/2}\) is homotopic to this bracket but generally different: for a rank-one Heisenberg current \(J\), ghost \(c\) and \(\kappa\ne0\), its value on \((c,(TJ)c)\) is \(3TJ/(4\kappa)\), while the specified bracket gives \(TJ/(2\kappa)\). This is a binary theorem on states.
known.antecedents: Elliott–Safronov (2018, preprint), Lemma 2.24; Bakalov–De Sole–Heluani–Kac, Chiral vs classical operad (2020), Theorem 5.2, arXiv:1812.05972.

known.title: The prescribed Heisenberg binary comparison is strict on all states
known.text: Over a characteristic-zero field at nonzero rank-one Heisenberg level \(\kappa\), use the universal polynomial complex \(Z=k[u_i:i\ge0]\otimes\Lambda(c_i:i\ge0)\), with undivided generators \(u_i=T^iJ\), \(c_i=T^ic\), and \(du_i=\kappa c_{i+1}\). For the two-copy Heisenberg comparison, its comparison homotopy \(h=h_{\mathrm{path}}-h_{\mathrm{cone}}\), projection \(P\), and independently defined geometric roof pairing, the comparison \(G_\lambda(a,b)=P[h(a)_\lambda h(b)]\) is zero for every pair of polynomial states. The corresponding pairings and specified secondary binary brackets agree strictly. This identifies the prescribed binary comparison; it does not identify an independently constructed higher geometric action.

known.antecedents: De Sole–Kac (2005), Theorems 2.5 and 3.9; Bakalov–Kac (2003), Theorem 6.9 and Wick formula (4.6). The Wick construction is known; the statement here is the all-state vanishing of the specified comparison.

known.title: The nonabelian binary comparison through energy two
known.text: For split \(\mathfrak{sl}_2\) over \(\mathbb Q[s,s^{-1}]\), with \([E,F]=H\), \((E,F)=1\), \((H,H)=2\), raw level \(s-2\) and shifted form \(s(\ ,\ )\), the specified secondary bracket on the universal polynomial affine Chevalley–Eilenberg states agrees with the secondary operation obtained from the separately defined \(\phi\)-endpoint pairing of the specified two-copy resolving construction, with its geometric roof interpretation on every ordered pair of total energy at most two. The comparison homotopy is zero on those pairs. This calculation also fixes the vanishing comparison homotopy on that finite-energy window. The full algebraic projected-field equality is stated separately.
known.antecedents: De Sole–Kac (2005), Theorem 3.9; Bakalov–Kac (2003), Theorem 6.9; Bakalov–De Sole–Heluani–Kac (2019), Lemma A.1 and Corollary A.2.

known.title: The two-copy affine field comparison on all algebraic states
known.text: For a finite-dimensional complex Lie algebra and universal affine vacua at invariant forms \(\kappa\) and \(-\kappa-\operatorname{Kill}\), the specified projected two-copy fields agree on every algebraic state. The theorem retains the absolute ghosts, algebraic energy sum, full regular coefficients, and prescribed contractions and projection. The primary equality requires no inverse form. When \(\beta=\kappa+\operatorname{Kill}/2\) is invertible, the secondary on all algebraic ghost jets is the average of the two endpoint extractions of the level-zero vertex-Poisson bracket. Some current-containing inputs fail the distinct residue comparison. Native supported operations and an independent geometric bulk action remain additional constructions.

known.title: Horizontal coherence, regular modules and a cobar inverse
known.text: For finite-dimensional complex \(\mathfrak g\) and any invariant symmetric form, the fixed-contraction rational gauge gives five literal four-position edges and a relative pentagon filler in their common recipient. Its nested expansions complete in displacements before localizing, and its choice of contraction and parameter section remains fixed. A translation-equivariant bar contraction also lifts a specified tensor-bar intertwiner horizontally, retaining finite support, whole-output bounds, and continuity on each fixed-denominator module. Fixed Tamari pulling triangulations carry strict units and coherent choices at every finite arity. Full bars admit evaluation-order families on permutohedra with literal nested block facets, source-unit restrictions, and interchange paths. Strict disjoint interchange is false, including on some individual pure-colour full-bar words; this does not invalidate the four-position relative pentagon. Unital comparison on finite PL subdivisions is also available for the same pointwise deletion maps, preserving endpoint families while allowing refinement. Ordered-cut-normalized mixed unary lifts and a relative gauge-comparison square also exist. Arbitrary prescribed unary boundaries have a stated relative obstruction, whose vanishing is not automatic. The faithful regular right module \(C\otimes N\) realizes the tensor and full-bar gauges with their parameter cells, units and collapse maps. An explicit algebraic cobar map \(F:\Omega X\to\Omega C\) retracts \(\Omega\mathrm{sh}\) exactly; its linear term is Alexander–Whitney and its output length on \(x\) is at most \(\phi(x)+1\). The other composite has a polynomial dg-algebra homotopy to the identity relative to \(\Omega\mathrm{sh}\). This gives the finite algebraic DCSH inverse, while the strict coalgebra inverse remains excluded. Changing the deletion maps, unrestricted completed duality and the comparison with actual native vacuum or endpoint operations remain separate. That comparison must retain the native coproduct, retraction, binary tensorator, connection and every unit and facet; fixed-factor-frame obstructions do not exclude changing endpoint frames.

questions.title: Positive type of the two-boundary kernel

question.title: Which charges give a positive kernel?
question.text: For a closed oriented surface of genus \(g\ge2\), let \(\mathcal T_g\) be its smooth marked Teichmüller space, with hyperbolic curvature \(-1\), and choose a base point \(o\). Let \(S\) be the classical Liouville action on the quasi-Fuchsian product, \(D(X,\overline Z)=8\pi(2g-2)-S(X,\overline Z)\), and let \(F_o\) be the base-point-normalized Hermitian holomorphic polarization of \(\Phi_o(X)=D(X,\overline o)\), so that \(F_o(X,\overline X)=\Phi_o(X)\) and \(F_o(X,\overline o)=0\). Determine \[\mathcal P_g=\left\{c\in[0,\infty):K_c(X,\overline Z)=\exp\!\left(\frac{cF_o(X,\overline Z)}{24\pi}\right)\text{ is of positive type on }\mathcal T_g\right\};\] positive type requires every finite matrix \((K_c(X_i,\overline{X_j}))\) to be positive semidefinite. The problem remains open at each fixed genus, including the positive unitary minimal charges and \(c\ge1\).

questions.why: Positive type turns the polarized action into a Hilbert-space pairing of holomorphic evaluation vectors. It is a global restriction on all finite configurations of complex structures, stronger than positivity of the diagonal metric or of a fixed collection of derivatives.

known.title: Nonminimal charges fail near large embedded discs
known.text: Fix a real charge \(0<c<1\) outside \(\{1-6/[p(p+1)]:p\in\mathbb Z,\ p\ge2\}\). There is a finite radius \(r_*(c)\) such that, on any closed curvature-\(-1\) hyperbolic surface of genus \(g\ge2\) with a point of injectivity radius at least \(r_*(c)\), the normalized Liouville kernel \(K_c=\exp(cF_o/(24\pi))\) has a negative finite derivative form and negative finite point matrices arbitrarily near that surface in \(\mathcal T_g\). Consequently \(c\notin\mathcal P_g\) for every sufficiently large integer \(g\). At \(c=1/4\), radius \(2400\) suffices: a compactly supported Beltrami family gives nine actual Teichmüller points and a quadratic form at most \(-837/1024\). These are exclusions for the closed-surface kernel; the negative Virasoro vacuum forms used as input are known.
source: chains/assault/q8-teichmuller-kernel-positivity/a/CHECK-1113-1140.md, S0-G, S0-H and S0-I; adoption lines
known.antecedents: Friedan–Qiu–Shenker, Details of the non-unitarity proof for highest weight representations of the Virasoro algebra (1986), Theorem 1; Neretin (2016), Corollary 1.3 and equation (3.4); Teo (2005), Theorems 3.5 and 4.3. The large-disc surfaces use the classical polygon geometry described by Stepanyants–Beardon–Paton–Krioukov (2024), §V, equations (18)–(21).

known.title: The universal quasicircle comparison
known.text: On the space of normalized exterior univalent maps \(\phi(w)=w+\sum_{n\ge1}\beta_nw^{-n}\) with Hilbert–Schmidt Grunsky operator \(B_\phi\), equivalently the corresponding Weil–Petersson quasicircles, the universal kernel \[\mathcal K_c(\phi,\overline\psi)=\exp\!\left(\frac{c}{2}\sum_{n\ge1}\frac{\operatorname{tr}((B_\psi^*B_\phi)^n)}n\right)\] uses ordinary trace-class products and is of positive type for real \(c\) exactly when \(c\in[1,\infty)\cup\{1-6/[p(p+1)]:p\in\mathbb Z,\ p\ge2\}\). Its Hilbert realization uses the Virasoro vacuum form modulo its radical, followed by completion; \(c=0\) gives a one-dimensional space. This comparison has the universal quasicircle domain, rather than the closed-surface domain \(\mathcal T_g\).

known.title: Calabi’s projective criterion at the Weil–Petersson scale
known.text: For \(g\ge2\) and \(c>0\), the normalized Liouville kernel \(K_c=\exp(cF_o/(24\pi))\) is of positive type on \(\mathcal T_g\) if and only if \((\mathcal T_g,c\omega_{\mathrm{WP}}/(24\pi))\) admits a holomorphic isometric immersion into projective Hilbert space. The conventions are \(\omega_{\mathrm{WP}}=iH_{j\bar k}\,dt_j\wedge d\bar t_k\), \(H(\mu,\nu)=\int\mu\overline\nu\,dA\), and \(\omega_{\mathrm{FS}}=i\partial\bar\partial\log\|v\|^2\). This is Calabi’s criterion together with analytic propagation for the globally defined kernel; the constant kernel at \(c=0\) is outside the metric-immersion assertion.
known.antecedents: Loi–Zedda (2017, preprint), Theorems 2.2.4 and 2.2.7, presenting Calabi’s criterion; Neeb–Ólafsson (2014), Appendix Theorem A.1(i).

known.title: Every two-point matrix is positive
known.text:
For the normalized kernel \(K_c=\exp(cF_o/(24\pi))\) on smooth marked \(\mathcal T_g\), \(g\ge2\), every two-point matrix is positive semidefinite for \(c\ge0\), and positive definite for \(c>0\) and distinct \(X,Z\). For \(c>0\) and \(X
e Z\), with \(
u=c/(24\pi)\) and Liouville diastasis \(D\), its determinant is \[K_c(X,\overline X)K_c(Z,\overline Z) igl(1-e^{-
u D(X,\overline Z)} igr)>0.\] Teo’s identity \(D=12\pi S_2\) gives \(D\ge0\), with equality only when \(X=Z\). This two-point inequality leaves larger matrices unrestricted.
known.antecedents: Teo, A different expression of the Weil–Petersson potential on the quasi-Fuchsian deformation space (2005), Definition 2.5, Theorem 4.3 and Corollary 4.4.

known.title: A positive realization would have infinite rank
known.text: For every \(g\ge2\) and real \(c>0\), the normalized Liouville kernel \(K_c=\exp(cF_o/(24\pi))\) on all of \(\mathcal T_g\) cannot simultaneously have positive type and finite rank. Thus any positive Hilbert realization must be infinite-dimensional. The obstruction uses the inverse-cubic Weil–Petersson metric along a one-node logarithmic plumbing collar and projective unitary monodromy; the rank-one constant kernel at \(c=0\) is allowed.
known.antecedents: Wolpert, Geometry of the Weil–Petersson completion of Teichmüller space (2005, preprint), Theorem 2(2), Corollary 4 and §5; Calabi rigidity as presented by Loi–Zedda (2017, preprint), Theorem 2.2.5.

known.title: The positivity set is a closed additive semigroup
known.text: For each fixed \(g\ge2\), the set \(\mathcal P_g=\{c\ge0:\exp(cF_o/(24\pi))\text{ is of positive type on }\mathcal T_g\}\) is closed in \([0,\infty)\), contains \(0\), and satisfies \(\mathcal P_g+\mathcal P_g\subseteq\mathcal P_g\). The identities \(K_0=1\) and \(K_{c+d}=K_cK_d\), together with the Schur product theorem, give these properties; they do not produce a positive charge.
known.antecedents: Aronszajn, Theory of Reproducing Kernels (1950), Part I §8, Theorem II; closedness of the positive semidefinite cone.

known.title: Full mixed jets through degree two
known.text:
For \(g\ge2\), real \(c>0\), and every point of \(\mathcal T_g\), the full mixed jet matrix of \(K_c=\exp(cF_o/(24\pi))\), indexed by all independent holomorphic derivatives of orders zero, one and two, is positive definite. Remove pure Taylor terms from a local potential by \[\Phi(z, ar z)\longmapsto\Phi(z, ar z)-\Phi(z,0)-\Phi(0, ar z)+\Phi(0,0).\] In Weil–Petersson normal coordinates and with \(
u=c/(24\pi)\), the quadratic block is \(
u^2(\delta_{ij}\delta_{kl}+\delta_{il}\delta_{kj})-
u R_{i ar j k ar l}\), where \(R=-\partial ar\partial g+g^{-1}\partial g\, ar\partial g\); the known Weil–Petersson curvature formula makes it strictly positive on symmetric tensors.

known.antecedents: Wolpert (2010, preprint), Geodesic-length functions and the Weil–Petersson curvature tensor, §5 equation (6), §4 Theorem 12; Liu–Sun–Yau (2008), Good Geometry on the Curve Moduli, Theorem 4.1.

known.title: Cubic jets along an immersed holomorphic curve
known.text: Let \(g\ge2\), \(c>0\), and \(x:(\mathbb D_\epsilon,0)\to\mathcal T_g\) be a holomorphic curve with \(x^{\prime}(0)\ne0\). For \(K_c=\exp(cF_o/(24\pi))\), the coefficient matrix of \(K_c(x(t),\overline{x(s)})\) on powers \(1,t,t^2,t^3\) is positive definite at zero. The assertion concerns one complex parameter, not the full several-variable cubic jet matrix.
known.antecedents: Teo (2005), fixed-group Grunsky construction; tracial Cauchy–Schwarz and symmetric tensor powers. Misra–Pal (2018), Theorem 2.2, is a related first-jet result.

known.title: An unramified covering multiplies the charge
known.text: Let \(p:\Sigma^{\prime}\to\Sigma\) be a fixed connected unramified orientation-preserving covering of closed marked surfaces of degree \(d\ge1\), with \(g\ge2\) and \(g^{\prime}=1+d(g-1)\). For the holomorphic pullback \(i_p:\mathcal T_g\to\mathcal T_{g^{\prime}}\), use base points \(o\) and \(i_p(o)\) in the normalized Liouville kernels. For every real \(c\), \[K_c^{(g^{\prime})}(i_p(X),\overline{i_p(Z)})=K_{dc}^{(g)}(X,\overline Z).\] Hence \(c\in\mathcal P_{g^{\prime}}\) implies \(dc\in\mathcal P_g\); division of a positive charge does not follow.
known.antecedents: Biswas–Nag (1996, preprint), Lemma 5.1 for characteristic-cover scaling; Kahn–Markovic (2008, preprint), introduction, remark before Theorem 1.1. The marked integral gives the factor for every fixed unramified cover.

known.title: The complete jet at one point detects positive type
known.text: For a connected finite-dimensional complex manifold \(M\) and a globally defined Hermitian holomorphic kernel \(K\) on \(M\times\overline M\), positive type on \(M\) is equivalent to positive type on one nonempty open subset, and to nonnegativity on every finitely supported vector of the complete Taylor matrix at one point. In local coordinates that matrix has entries \(\partial^\alpha\bar\partial^\beta K/(\alpha!\beta!)\), including the constant term and every order. In particular this criterion applies to \(K_c=\exp(cF_o/(24\pi))\) on \(\mathcal T_g\), \(g\ge2\); no finite jet cutoff suffices by this theorem.
known.antecedents: Neeb–Ólafsson, Reflection Positivity and Conformal Symmetry (2014), Appendix Theorem A.1(i); Loi–Zedda (2017, preprint), Theorems 2.2.4 and 2.2.6.

known.title: Every fixed jet order is eventually positive
known.text: For each fixed point \(X\in\mathcal T_g\), \(g\ge2\), and each fixed integer \(m\ge0\), the full degree-at-most-\(m\) coefficient matrix of \(K_c=\exp(cF_o/(24\pi))\) at \(X\) is positive definite for all sufficiently large real \(c\). The threshold may depend on both \(X\) and \(m\). The same assertion holds locally for the exponential of the polarization of any real-analytic strictly plurisubharmonic potential; it gives no single charge that works for all orders.
known.antecedents: The leading Fock coefficients and stability of finite positive matrices; the all-order framework is Loi–Zedda (2017, preprint), Theorems 2.2.4 and 2.2.6.

known.title: The regularized mixed Grunsky identity
known.text: Fix a base surface \(o\in\mathcal T_g\), \(g\ge2\), uniformized by a torsion-free cocompact group \(\Gamma\), and the fixed conformal end of its Bers slice. On the Bergman Hilbert space \(H=A^2(\mathbb D)\) of holomorphic one-forms, the actual Grunsky operators \(B_X:\overline H\to H\) form a norm-holomorphic \(\Gamma\)-equivariant family with \(B_o=0\) and \(\|B_X\|<1\). With the fundamental-domain trace \(\tau_\Gamma\) normalized by \(\tau_\Gamma(1)=g-1\), the base-point-normalized Liouville kernel satisfies \[K_c(X,\overline Z)=\exp\!\left(\frac{c}{2}\sum_{n\ge1}\frac{\tau_\Gamma((B_XB_Z^*)^n)}n\right).\] The series converges absolutely and locally uniformly on the entire smooth marked product \(\mathcal T_g\times\overline{\mathcal T_g}\); for real \(c\) it is Hermitian. This identity uses the finite group trace, and makes no positive-type assertion.
known.antecedents: Teo (2005), Corollary 2.4, Definition 2.5, Proposition 2.7, Lemma 3.2 and Theorem 4.3; Takhtajan–Teo (2002, preprint), Liouville action and Weil–Petersson metric on deformation spaces.

known.title: The trace belongs to the equivariant operator algebra
known.text: For a torsion-free cocompact surface group \(\Gamma\) of genus \(g\ge2\) acting on the Bergman space \(H=A^2(\mathbb D)\) of holomorphic one-forms, integration of the diagonal operator kernel over a fundamental domain defines a finite positive trace on \(\operatorname{End}_\Gamma(H)\). It satisfies \(\tau_\Gamma(1)=g-1\), \(|\tau_\Gamma(A)|\le(g-1)\|A\|\), and \(\tau_\Gamma(AC)=\tau_\Gamma(CA)\) for bounded equivariant endomorphisms. In contrast, a nonzero actual closed-surface Grunsky product \(BB^*\) on the full disc Bergman space has infinite ordinary trace.
known.antecedents: Jones, Enseignement Mathématique 69 (2023), Corollary 3.6 and Theorem 4.8; Teo (2005), §2.2.2.

known.title: The whole intertwiner ball is too large
known.text: For a torsion-free cocompact surface group \(\Gamma\) of genus \(g\ge2\), let \(H=A^2(\mathbb D)\), with its one-form action and trace \(\tau_\Gamma(1)=g-1\). On the entire open unit ball of bounded \(\Gamma\)-intertwiners \(A:\overline H\to H\), the kernel \[J_c(A,\overline B)=\exp\!\left(\frac{c}{2}\sum_{n\ge1}\frac{\tau_\Gamma((AB^*)^n)}n\right)\] fails positive type for every real \(c>0\). A matrix corner with normalized exponent \(a=c(g-1)/(2n)\in(0,1/2)\) gives the known rank-two Wallach coefficient matrix \(\begin{pmatrix}a^2&a\\a&a(2a+1)\end{pmatrix}\), which is negative on \((-1/a,1)\). This corner lies in the full intertwiner ball; no realization of it by the Grunsky operators of closed surfaces is asserted.
known.antecedents: Jones (2023), Theorem 3.4, Corollary 3.6, Theorem 4.8 and Notes 4.9(2); Nakahama, SIGMA 18 (2022), 033, Theorem 2.9 and equation (2.11).

questions.title: Moving centralizers and line fusion

question.title: Compare the transverse bar with all induced line states
question.text: For a finite-dimensional nonabelian Lie algebra over a characteristic-zero field, with invariant symmetric level form \(\kappa\) and nondegenerate \(\beta=\kappa+\operatorname{Kill}/2\), construct a normalized comparison between the moving affine centralizer, its restricted bar dual in the transverse line direction, and line fusion on affine Weyl modules induced from finite-dimensional charge tops. Specify the positive-weight and length completions and preserve the full nonlinear translation homotopy, the prescribed product homotopy, native products, the vacuum and both ordered collision maps on all induced states. On three modules, identify the associativity homotopies with the Knizhnik–Zamolodchikov connection and its descendants. Prove continuity for each source energy, output cutoff and Laurent coefficient, including words containing product entries.

questions.why: The Casimir residue on a charge top fixes only the first part of the comparison. The line construction must also carry the nonlinear homotopies and all descendants through collision and fusion, on explicitly specified completions where the comparison maps and homotopies are continuous.

known.title: A continuous native-product bar comparison at one position
known.text: Let \(\mathfrak g\) be a finite-dimensional complex reductive Lie algebra, \(\kappa\) an invariant symmetric form, and \(\beta=\kappa+\operatorname{Kill}/2\) nondegenerate. At one position, use the universal polynomial affine Chevalley–Eilenberg complex \(Z\), with positive PBW weight \(2n+1\) on the current \(j_n=x_{-n-1}\) and ghost \(c_n\), and the completion of its reduced tensor bar by that weight. Starting from the opposite regular associative PBW product, there is a coalgebra change of coordinates continuous in both directions that gives a strictly unital augmented \(A_\infty\) structure whose binary operation is exactly the native normally ordered product. Its inverse Taylor terms vanish above arity \(4e\) at positive energy \(e\), and above arity one at energy zero. The continuous finite-support graded dual of this completed bar is quasi-isomorphic to the polynomial line algebra \(Y_\beta\), with no completion in zero-mode length. The full translation and Sugawara operators extend to continuous higher bar coderivations and are intertwined with the line operators. This one-position comparison does not identify the prescribed product homotopy or supply geometric collisions and an induced-module functor.
known.antecedents: Chevalley–Eilenberg (1948), Theorem 24.1; Loday–Vallette (2012), Theorems 10.3.6 and 10.3.8; Getzler (2026), Proposition 2, Corollary 1 and Theorem 3. The regular point-duality construction is an antecedent.

known.title: An algebraic inverse can leave the continuous bar dual
known.text: For split \(\mathfrak{sl}_2\) over a characteristic-zero field, with raw level \(\lambda\), \((E,F)=1\), \((H,H)=2\), and \(s=\lambda+2\ne0\), use universal polynomial states and positive PBW weight \(2n+1\) on current and ghost modes. Let \(m\) be the native product, \(\star\) the product transported from the regular PBW model, and choose the binary coordinate primitive \(H_{\mathrm{en}}(m-\star)\), where \(H_{\mathrm{en}}\) is the energy retraction homotopy. On suspended words \(w_n=\sigma J_E\mid(\sigma c_0^H)^{\otimes n}\), take the identity-linear bar map with this binary component and all Taylor components of arity greater than two zero; it satisfies \[F(w_0)=w_0,\quad F(w_n)=w_n-s^{-1}w_{n-1}\ (n\ge1),\qquad F^{-1}(w_n)=\sum_{j=0}^ns^{-j}w_{n-j}\ (n\ge0).\] Every \(w_n\) has energy one, and its inverse has a nonzero one-letter term \(s^{-n}\sigma J_E\). Thus this particular algebraic inverse is not continuous in the positive-weight completion and its transpose does not preserve the finite-support dual.
known.antecedents: Loday–Vallette (2012), Proposition 10.2.3; Atiyah–Macdonald (1969), Chapter 1, Exercises 2(i) and 5(i).

known.title: Ordinary derived cochains lose Wilson tensor products
known.text: Let \(k\) have characteristic zero, let \(\mathfrak g=\mathfrak{sl}_2(k)\), and let \(R\) be its defining two-dimensional representation. The ordinary Chevalley–Eilenberg complex \(C^*(\mathfrak g;R)\) is acyclic, whereas \(C^*(\mathfrak g;R\otimes R)\) has a copy of \(k\) in degrees zero and three. Therefore the functor to ordinary derived \(C^*(\mathfrak g;k)\)-modules cannot be a faithful strong monoidal realization of these Wilson charges: the derived tensor of the two zero images is zero, while the coefficient tensor has nonzero cohomology.
known.antecedents: Chevalley–Eilenberg (1948), Theorem 24.1, pp. 117–119.

questions.title: Fields from a completed coefficient dual

question.title: Fields from a completed coefficient dual
question.text: Construct an independently defined field recipient for the completed coefficient dual, with both binary orders, curvature, both vacuum insertions, normal derivatives, and nonconsecutive collisions. Compare its module tensor product with the transported coefficient tensor. The native \(\mathfrak{gl}_2\) test modulo \(\hbar^3\) must retain composite marks and actual evaluation. Polar field existence alone does not identify that native map.

questions.why: The coefficient equivalence already exists. Field extraction must retain the extension classes and operations that the equivalence transports.

questions.title: A common transverse recipient

question.title: A common transverse recipient
question.text: Construct an independently defined native coefficient recipient on a curve times a real line that preserves the local vacuum, interval homotopies, all collision faces and Weiss descent. Compare the checked three-position contact-image cofiber with that recipient while preserving its marked polar-vacuum extension, complete relative contacts and proper-pair maps. Extend the comparison beyond its finite-pole and polynomial-state domains, and settle the original unscaled zero-inclusive target; the invertible-level construction does not supply it. Extend the computed unrestricted scalar current cohomology and its evaluation to the required state-valued and topological domains without discarding the three escaping modules. Extend independent-root forest calculus to nonroot landings, dependent normals and all native substitutions.

questions.why: Actual contact images now supply a marked three-position comparison at invertible level. Its finite domains, nonzero source kernel and chosen recipient leave the independent all-position and zero-inclusive native comparisons to be constructed. The unrestricted scalar escaping modules remain part of the original domain.

known.title: Global scalar currents and the escaping summands
known.text: Let \(Y_\rho=\mathbb R^2\times\Omega_\rho\), where \(\Omega_\rho=\{(u,v):|u|,|v|,|u+v|<\rho\}\), and use the original scalar distributional relative-current complex, with distribution order finite on every compact. Its algebraic second cohomology is \[H^2(I(Y_\rho))=E_u\oplus E_s\oplus E_v\oplus j_A P\oplus j_S P,\qquad s=u+v,\] where \(P=\mathbb C[\partial_u,\partial_v]\delta\) and each \(E_x\) is the cokernel of the tangential Dolbeault differential on locally finite principal-part coefficient families. The escaping summands vanish on every smaller radius; their respective normal coordinates act invertibly. The forest sum is exactly the largest submodule on which both \(u\) and \(v\) act locally nilpotently, and its section is unique among polynomial-Weyl-linear sections. The original scalar vacuum evaluation is an isomorphism in degrees zero and one and has exactly the forest image in degree two, with the three escaping modules as cokernel. Thus its old global quasi-isomorphism assertion is false. Evaluation is a quasi-isomorphism into the different finite-normal contact complex and in the specified normal-germ limit. The calculation is algebraic and scalar; it supplies no continuous or Hausdorff splitting, state-valued extension or full native recipient.

known.title: Finite rooted forests and a necessary marked quotient
known.text: On the admitted independent external-product domains, relative multiplication gives every finite rooted forest with all contact terms, holomorphic normal action, root-compatible nested cuts, transported relabelling and both occupied-vacuum formulas. Nonroot landings, dependent normals and height-wall crossings need additional maps. For the specified algebraic finite-normal-order sheet, the connecting image is exactly \(\hbar J_S(P)\), while double-bulk operations generate \(\hbar^2J_S(P)\); zero level, nonzero polynomial scalar level and the formal power-series ring have distinct conclusions. A normal-linear polar-vacuum lift preserving the specified regular face forces a nonzero class in quotient or cofiber \(H^1\) annihilated by both normal coordinates. The complete two-map comparison forces two principal-part copies. This excludes the stated nonnegative finite-stage sheet quotients with tangentially injective degree-one modules. It does not exclude all native intermediate recipients or prove that the necessary torsion classes suffice to construct the lift.

known.title: A marked comparison from two native contact images
known.text: For three positions, the actual reversed outer-sheet and pair-sheet contact images define a direct-sum cofiber \(E\) of the original current complex \(F\). Write \(\mathcal P\) for the joint principal-part module, with finite pole orders on each input and polynomial Heisenberg state coefficients. Its cohomology satisfies \(H^k(E)=H^k(F)\) for \(k\ne2\), including the full old \(H^1\), and \[H^2(E)=H^2(F)/\hbar\bigl(J_A(\mathcal P)+J_S(\mathcal P)\bigr).\] The full current domain of \(F\) is unchanged; finite bounds concern the added operation inputs. No assertion that these forests exhaust the native second cohomology is needed. At each nonzero polynomial level, and after formal \(\hbar\) inversion, an actual normal-linear comparison exists on the stated finite analytic-pole and polynomial-state stages. It preserves the nonsplit marked vacuum extension, both complete polar-vacuum placements, the spectator connection and the existing proper-pair roofs. The exact chain kernel of the comparison \(\Theta_\kappa\) is the regular left-vacuum block. Both \(\Theta_\kappa\) and its stated geometric composite \(\Theta_\kappa\Psi\) kill a nonzero first-cohomology class of their source and have no homotopy left inverse. No entire chain-kernel formula for the composite or cohomological-kernel classification is asserted. The integral comparison scales the marked current map by \(\hbar\), and an unscaled zero-inclusive attachment remains obstructed in this cofiber. Base-changing its free image modules at zero differs from forming the images of the specialized zero operations. Selecting these contact sources and this cofiber is part of the construction. Independent all-position native origin, products, substitutions, descent and uniform completed-state estimates remain open.

The rooted linear-diagram comparison now retains the ordered collision maps and kills the primary unmixed two-vacuum class; the uniform-source secondary class \(\ell\rho^{\prime}\) remains. known.title: Surjective base change and the tame cocycle subcategory
known.text: Over \(\mathbb C\), retain the nonzero-level rank-one Heisenberg boundary, the exterior actor \(B=\Lambda(\epsilon)\) with \(|\epsilon|=1\) and \(d\epsilon=T\epsilon=0\), ordinary algebraic tensors and localization at state quasi-isomorphisms. For a surjective base arrow \(a:d\to d^{\prime}\) in the specified Heisenberg action comparison, let \(G_d^a\) be the full subcategory where the dg vertex ideal generated by \(h(\ker a)\) is acyclic. Quotienting by that ideal proves \[N G_{d^{\prime}}\simeq N G_d^a,\] preserving both cocycle legs, all refinements and every admissible target link. A base section retracts the full transition and makes it injective on components and all based homotopy groups. The displayed split object and specified pullbacks are tame. The remaining inclusion \(N G_d^a\to N G_d\) is still undecided, including higher homotopy even if every component meets the tame subcategory. A functorial incoming tame refinement \(c(g)\to g\) would suffice and can be made surjective by a mapping-path construction. Relative free/PBW exactness is one possible method, not a necessary or equivalent criterion. The ideal-valued monotonicity test only excludes outgoing arrows to tame objects; it excludes neither incoming refinements nor zigzags. Non-surjective and full required transitions, \(\lambda_B\), the separate nilpotent inclusion and the actual \(q_B\) comparison remain open.

statements.title: A free field with two independent parameters
statements.text: Over \(\mathbb C\), let \(\kappa,\lambda\in\mathbb C\) and give \(V=\mathbb C[x_1,x_2,\ldots]\), \(Tx_r=rx_{r+1}\), the Wick contraction \(P(u)=\kappa u^{-2}+\lambda u^{-1}\). Its exchange satisfies \(S(u)(x_1\otimes x_1)=x_1\otimes x_1-2\lambda u^{-1}1\otimes1\), and its ordinary unital geometric point modules with all marked collisions are exactly the smooth modules with \([J_m,J_n]=(\kappa m\delta_{m+n,0}+\lambda\varepsilon(m)\delta_{m+n,-1})1\), where \(\varepsilon(m)=1\) for \(m\ge0\) and \(-1\) otherwise. The curved dual has zero differential and curvature \(\sum_{r\ge1}(\kappa r e_r+\lambda e_{r-1})e_{-r}\) on exterior cochains completed by finite negative-mode cutoffs separately in each exterior degree, with finite positive-mode support at each cutoff. For any two contractions of this form, the primitive field map \(V_{P+Q}\to V_P\otimes V_Q\) preserves fields and exchange and adds the contraction parameters; it is not a fixed-level fusion coproduct.

statements.title: Fock modules and rational coinvariants
statements.text: Over \(\mathbb C\) at \(\kappa\ne0\), consider Heisenberg modules with \([a_m,a_n]=m\kappa\delta_{m+n,0}\), each positive mode locally nilpotent, and sufficiently high positive modes annihilating each vector. The assignment \(E\mapsto\mathcal F(E)=E[x_1,x_2,\ldots]\), with \(a_{-m}=x_m\), \(a_m=m\kappa\partial_{x_m}\) and \(a_0=A_E\), is an exact equivalence from \(\mathbb C[a_0]\)-modules, and negative-current coinvariants recover \(E\). At finitely many distinct complex points, the derived coinvariants of the algebraic tensor product of these Fock modules under rational currents vanishing at infinity are \(\bigotimes_iE_i\) in degree zero. For finite-dimensional \(E_i\), their coinvariant connection is \(d+\kappa^{-1}\sum_{i<j}A_iA_j\,d\log(p_i-p_j)\); on scalar-charge dual fibres the positive half-exchange is \(e^{\pi i\alpha\beta/\kappa}\) followed by the flip, with normalized associator equal to one.

statements.title: Grading changes the derived endomorphisms
statements.text: For the algebraic Heisenberg mode algebra \(A_\kappa\) over \(\mathbb C\), with \(\kappa\ne0\), put \(\mathfrak n_-=\bigoplus_{m\ge1}\mathbb Ca_{-m}\), \(W=A_\kappa\otimes_{U(\mathfrak n_-)}\mathbb C\) and \(R=\mathbb C[a_0]\). With \(\deg a_n=n\), internally graded derived Hom, summed over internal degrees but retaining full products within each homogeneous component, gives a formal endomorphism dg algebra with value \(R\). In the ordinary unbounded derived category of all algebraic \(A_\kappa\)-modules, \(\operatorname{Ext}^0(W,W)=R\), \(\operatorname{Ext}^1(W,W)=(\prod_{m\ge1}V_m)/(\bigoplus_{m\ge1}V_m)\), where \(V_m=a_mR[a_m,a_{m+1},\ldots]\), and every other degree vanishes. For every polynomial Fock module \(\mathcal F(E)\), full \(\operatorname{RHom}(W,\mathcal F(E))\) vanishes, whereas derived negative-current coinvariants equal \(E[0]\).

statements.title: The Gaussian bulk and its boundary current
statements.text: On \(\mathbb C\times\mathbb R_{\ge0}\), take the Gaussian abelian Chern–Simons observable complex over \(\mathbb C\), with numerical \(k=\hbar\kappa\ne0\), pairing \(-\kappa(2\pi i)^{-1}\int\alpha\wedge\beta\), and boundary condition \(j^*\alpha\in dz\wedge\Omega_c^\bullet\). Its carrier is the direct sum over field number of completed projective bornological symmetric powers, realized by compact smooth kernels satisfying that boundary condition in every variable. The rotation-finite boundary cohomology is the universal rank-one Heisenberg vertex algebra \(V_k\), while interior cohomology is an exterior algebra on one degree-one class. With orientation \(dx\wedge dy\wedge dt\), the outward-oriented sphere operation and the generator \(\xi\) normalized by \(\iota_{J_0}\xi=1\), the bulk bracket is \(\{\xi,\xi\}=2\pi i/k\), and the corresponding finite-jet vacuum cohomology has algebraic secondary pairing \(1/k\).

statements.title: Vacuum extensions detect the Heisenberg level
statements.text: Over \(\mathbb C\) at \(\kappa\ne0\), restrict the polynomial Heisenberg Fock construction to finite-dimensional \(\mathbb C[t]\)-modules with nilpotent \(t\), where \(a_0=t\), and transport the product by \(\mathcal F(M)\star\mathcal F(N)=\mathcal F(M\otimes N)\). Prescribe the conformal-block connection \(d-(T_M\otimes T_N/\kappa)\,dz/z\) on these chosen coefficient spaces, with the ordinary associator; the positive half-exchange is \(\operatorname{flip}\exp(\pi iT_M\otimes T_N/\kappa)\). On the marked vacuum extension \(J=\mathbb C[t]/(t^2)\), with its inclusion and quotient maps \(i:\mathbb C\to J\), \(p:J\to\mathbb C\), normalized by \(i(1)=t\), \(p(1)=1\), \(p(t)=0\), and \(n=ip\), positive pure braid is \(1+(2\pi i/\kappa)n\otimes n\). A complex-linear exact strong braided equivalence preserving this exact marked extension and its unit identification between levels \(\kappa,\kappa'\ne0\) therefore requires \(\kappa=\kappa'\), although the ambient associative algebra \(\operatorname{RHom}_{\mathbb C[t]}(\mathbb C,\mathbb C)\simeq\Lambda(\epsilon)\), \(|\epsilon|=1\), is unchanged.

statements.title: A comparison preserving the vacuum and its operations
statements.text: For nonzero-level Heisenberg modules over \(\mathbb C\), construct an independently defined comparison between negative-current coinvariants and the degreewise completed curved cochain transform on one common localized category, preserving the marked vacuum, translation, rational collision maps and logarithmic transport. Extend the Gaussian endpoint construction to nilpotent vacuum extensions with compatible transport and framing: for two unit charges at level three, increasing-normal-coordinate graph transport around a positive full turn gives \(e^{-2\pi i/3}\), whereas positive Fock continuation gives \(e^{2\pi i/3}\). An opposite-transport functor or a comparison with the reverse braided target remains to be constructed, together with the comparison preserving mixed operations of independent local bulk observables. The outgoing collision normalization is taken on the positive-real branch in this phase test.

statements.title: Siegel–Weil for the hyperbolic genus
statements.text: Let \(V\) be a strongly rational holomorphic vertex operator algebra over \(\mathbb C\), with its conformal vector, algebraic graded direct-sum states, a chosen Cartan subalgebra of \(V_1\), strongly rational Heisenberg commutant \(C\), and associated positive-definite even lattice of rank \(r\ge3\). Write \(c=c(V)\), let \(\mathcal H(V)\) be its hyperbolic genus, let \(G_W\) be the finite image of the Cartan-preserving automorphisms of \(W\) on its associated lattice, and put \(m(V)=\sum_{[W]\in\mathcal H(V)}|G_W|^{-1}\). For \(r>4\) and \(\tau\) in the upper half-plane, \[\frac{1}{m(V)}\sum_{[W]\in\mathcal H(V)}\frac{\operatorname{ch}_W(\tau)}{|G_W|}=\sum_{\gamma\in\Gamma_\infty\backslash\operatorname{SL}_2(\mathbb Z)}\varepsilon(\gamma)^c\frac{\operatorname{ch}_C(\gamma\tau)}{\eta(\gamma\tau)^r},\qquad \Gamma_\infty=\{\pm T^n:n\in\mathbb Z\}.\] Here \(\eta\) is the Dedekind eta function and \(\varepsilon\) its standard multiplier, with metaplectic lifts when required; the sum is absolutely and locally uniformly convergent. At \(r=3,4\), multiply each summand by \(\operatorname{Im}(\gamma\tau)^t\), continue meromorphically from \(\operatorname{Re}t>1-r/4\), and evaluate at \(t=0\): the standard section specified by the real Gaussian and finite lattice-coset characteristic functions is regular there and has the same value, with the metaplectic convention at rank three. The proof uses the positive nonvacuum commutant weights supplied by Dong–Sun–Wang’s 2026 preprint; assuming those weights are strictly positive is an explicit alternative hypothesis. For this holomorphic class this establishes, in the absolutely convergent range \(r>4\), the character identity of Möller–Rayhaun, arXiv:2408.07117 (2024), Conjecture 5.7; at \(r=3,4\) the identity holds for the specified continuation. The arithmetic Siegel–Weil theorems are known inputs.
statements.antecedents: Möller–Rayhaun (2024), arXiv:2408.07117, Conjecture 5.7, Theorem 4.7 and Corollary 4.11; van Ekeren–Möller–Scheithauer (2015, preprint), Theorem 4.2; Dong–Sun–Wang (2026, preprint), arXiv:2611.12417, Theorem 3 and Corollary 5.3; Opitz (2018), Theorem 3.7.2; Kudla (2001, preprint), arXiv:math/0110236, Theorem 4.1(i) and Proposition 4.22.

statements.title: Characters, discriminant gluings and genus mass
statements.text: For a strongly rational holomorphic complex vertex operator algebra \(V\) with a chosen Cartan of \(V_1\), strongly rational Heisenberg commutant \(C\), positive-definite even associated lattice \(L\) of rank \(r\ge3\), and positive nonvacuum \(C\)-module weights as supplied by Dong–Sun–Wang (2026), put \(D=L^*/L\), let \(K\subset O(D)\) be the image of \(\operatorname{Aut}(C)\) on its simple modules under the opposite-discriminant identification, and set \(m_L=\sum_{[M]\in\operatorname{gen}(L)}|O(M)|^{-1}\). Every discriminant isometry \(\phi:D_M\to D\) gives the holomorphic extension \(W_{M,\phi}=\bigoplus_{a\in D_M}C_{\phi(a)}\otimes V_{M+a}\), on algebraic ordinary states, and the isomorphism classes over \(M\) are \(K\backslash\operatorname{Iso}(D_M,D)/O(M)\). For characters on the upper half-plane, let \(G_W\) be the full finite image of the Cartan-preserving automorphisms on the associated lattice, and set \(m(V)=\sum_{[W]\in\mathcal H(V)}|G_W|^{-1}\) over the hyperbolic genus. Then \[m(V)=\frac{|O(D)|}{|K|}m_L,\qquad \frac{1}{m(V)}\sum_{[W]}\frac{\operatorname{ch}_W}{|G_W|}=\eta^{-r}f^T\Theta_{\mathrm{av}},\qquad \Theta_{\mathrm{av}}=\frac{1}{m_L|O(D)|}\sum_{[M]}\frac{1}{|O(M)|}\sum_{\sigma\in O(D)}\sigma\theta_M,\] where \(f=(\operatorname{ch}_{C_a})_{a\in D}\) and \(\theta_M\) is the vector of lattice-coset theta series. The mass formula itself is known from Moriwaki and Möller–Rayhaun; the character contraction retains the entire discriminant symmetrization and the kernels of the lattice actions.
statements.antecedents: Moriwaki (2021, revised preprint), Theorem 4.16; Möller–Rayhaun (2024), Theorem 4.7, Corollary 4.11, Proposition 4.15 and Corollary 4.16; van Ekeren–Möller–Scheithauer (2015, preprint), Theorem 4.2; Dong–Sun–Wang (2026, preprint), Theorem 3 and Corollary 5.3.

statements.title: The hyperbolic average on marked curves in every genus
statements.text: Let \(V\), of central charge \(c=c(V)\), be strongly rational and holomorphic over \(\mathbb C\), with a chosen Cartan of \(V_1\), strongly rational Heisenberg commutant \(C\), associated positive-definite even lattice \(L\) of rank \(r\ge3\), and positive nonvacuum commutant weights supplied by Dong–Sun–Wang (2026), or assumed explicitly. For each \(g\ge1\), use ordinary algebraic modules, restricted duals, invariant forms with vacuum norm one, and a marked sphere with \(g\) disjoint paired handle sewings and an extra vacuum insertion. If \(B_g\) is the rank-one Heisenberg vacuum sewing series with constant term one, \(C_g\) the commutant vector built from its own creation and evaluation intertwiners, \(f_{C,g}=B_g^{-(c-r)}C_g\), and \(\Phi_{W,g}=B_g^{-c}Z_{W,g}\), then \[\frac{1}{m(V)}\sum_{[W]\in\mathcal H(V)}\frac{\Phi_{W,g}}{|G_W|}=f_{C,g}^T\Theta_{\mathrm{av}}^{(g)}=\kappa_{r,g}^{-1}f_{C,g}^TE_{D,g}(\Omega,0),\qquad \kappa_{r,g}=\begin{cases}1&r>g+1,\\2&r\le g+1.\end{cases}\] Here \(m(V)=\sum|G_W|^{-1}\) uses full effective lattice stabilizers, \(D=L^*/L\), and \(\Theta_{\mathrm{av}}^{(g)}\) is the mass-normalized lattice-genus theta vector symmetrized by one \(O(D)\)-element acting simultaneously on all handles. The Eisenstein vector uses the standard Gaussian and finite lattice-coset characteristic functions, parameter \(s=(r-g-1)/2+2t\), and continuation from \(r/2+2\operatorname{Re}t>g+1\); its value at zero is regular. Equality is coefficientwise in the finitely many plumbing parameters, locally analytic on disjoint-disc sewing domains, and continues as an equality of sections on marked smooth curves, compatibly with the actual geometric changes of coordinates, factorization and pinching, using the same VOA, lattice and gluing label on every component before averaging products. The commutant factor is defined on curve charts; only the theta factor is defined on full Siegel space. The arithmetic equality, including its factor, is known from Kudla at even rank and Li’s metaplectic theorem at odd rank.
statements.antecedents: Kudla, Some extensions of the Siegel–Weil formula (1992), Theorem I.2; Li (2023, revised preprint), arXiv:2110.07457, Theorem 2.2.9 and Remark 2.2.12; Damiolini–Gibney–Tarasca (2019, preprint), Theorem 8.5.1; Gui (2023, revised preprint), Theorem 13.1; Tuite–Welby (2023, preprint), equations (99)–(104), (114)–(115), (133) and §7.2; Carpi–Codogni (2026, preprint), Theorems 7.3–7.4 and Proposition 7.6; Dong–Sun–Wang (2026, preprint), Theorem 3 and Corollary 5.3.

statements.title: Averaging does not preserve scalar sewing products
statements.text: For the positive-definite even unimodular rank-sixteen genus \(\{E_8\oplus E_8,D_{16}^{+}\}\), let \(p=286/691\), \(q=405/691\) be the normalized inverse-orthogonal-group weights and write \(A_g=p\theta_{E_8\oplus E_8}^{(g)}+q\theta_{D_{16}^{+}}^{(g)}\), \(\Delta_g=\theta_{E_8\oplus E_8}^{(g)}-\theta_{D_{16}^{+}}^{(g)}\). On a block diagonal in Siegel space, \[A_{g+h}\big|_{g+h\to g,h}-A_gA_h=pq\Delta_g\Delta_h.\] The \(4+4\) restriction has nonzero coefficient \(3085190905724928000/477481\), detected by the ordered \(D_4\) Gram coefficients \(7257600\) and \(2096640\). For actual lattice-VOA curve amplitudes, with the same vacuum plumbing factor removed and a common determinant-line trivialization, the corresponding \(5+5\) separating coefficient is \(759006325862823886848000/477481\). The valid average retains the same lattice label on both factors before summing; scalar multiplication of separately averaged amplitudes fails.

statements.title: The masses of the rank-four genus with weight-one algebra of type C
statements.text: For the strongly rational holomorphic complex vertex operator algebra of central charge \(24\) whose weight-one Lie algebra is of type \(C_4\) at affine level \(10\), the associated lattice is \(\sqrt{10}D_4\). Its lattice-genus mass is \(1/1152\), and its hyperbolic-VOA-genus mass, using full effective Cartan-preserving lattice groups, is \(1/384\): \(|O(D_4)|=1152\), \(|W(C_4)|=384\), and the discriminant index is three.
statements.antecedents: Betsumiya–Lam–Shimakura (2022, preprint), §5.10, Propositions 5.28–5.29; Möller–Rayhaun (2024), Table 2. Orthogonal and Weyl group orders are standard.

statements.title: The rank-four character
statements.text: For the strongly rational holomorphic complex vertex operator algebra of central charge \(24\) with weight-one Lie algebra of type \(C_4\) at level \(10\), strongly rational Cartan Heisenberg commutant and associated lattice \(\sqrt{10}D_4\), the normalized hyperbolic-genus character average is \[j(\tau)-708=q^{-1}+36+196884q+21493760q^2+\cdots,\qquad q=e^{2\pi i\tau}.\] The genus has a single holomorphic isomorphism class.

statements.title: A coefficient-native category of charged endpoints
statements.text: For the Gaussian charged-endpoint construction, a chosen propagator defines a bounded dg product \(B_P\) on the compact smooth native carrier. The finite-free singleton coefficient category has all bounded \(B_P\)-linear maps, strict composition and units, balanced tensor and finite charged duals satisfying both triangles. Collar and moment functors are quasi-equivalences at this singleton scope. A specified continuous product bar contracts by a conjugated Euler homotopy, and smooth position families carry the actual differential-form correction. Separately, ordinary tensor descends in the split module-homotopy category, the polynomial tower has all-arity units on every dg \(E\)-module, and polynomial Wick maps have transported-operator corrections on the stated large-separation Laurent domain. These are coefficient and module-homotopy comparisons: the charged graded-free kernel remains non-K-flat in the ordinary derived category. Two compact sources of charges \(q,-q\) in one ball give a concrete failure of the naive all-position map to one energy-completed multipole point. Other recipients remain possible. The later point-derived local-cohomology coring and all-charge hybrid diagonal coring are specified separately below. The full native cut actor, occupied vacua, common collision/separation completion, nonsplit geometric left endpoint, invariant geometric balanced coring and physical sewing remain open.

statements.title: Point-derived duality and the separate all-charge coring
statements.text: For the specified exterior-point and polynomial oscillator coefficient algebras, the genuine ordinary derived adjunction has kernel \(R\Gamma_{(t)}B\), \(B=k[t]\), with an explicit Čech counit, coproduct, idempotence and triangle identities. Its image is the \(t\)-power-supported derived sector. A separate hybrid coefficient enhancement admits every algebraic unbounded charged complex and all graded module-linear maps, with the diagonal Koszul coring and balanced triangles. The charged graded-free kernel remains non-K-flat over the exterior algebra; its ordinary and derived tensors are different. The full oscillator algebra has an actual derived unit roof. The product-bar homotopy has total-count bounds on the stated polynomial, fixed-field native and oscillator-energy domains; an arbitrary completion mixing infinitely many counts in one coefficient needs a further estimate.
